This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $r\geq 3$. For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $G$ let $\tau(G)$ denote the covering number (or transversal number), the minimum size of a set of vertices which includes at least one from each edge in $G$.
Determine the best possible $t$ such that, if $G$ is an $r$-uniform hypergraph $G$ where every subgraph $G'$ on at most $3r-3$ vertices has $\tau(G')\leq 1$, we have $\tau(G)\leq t$.
#616: [Er99]
graph theory
Erdős, Hajnal, and Tuza [EHT91] proved that this $t$ satisfies\[\frac{3}{16}r+\frac{7}{8}\leq t \leq \frac{1}{5}r.\]

 The bounds displayed here from [EHT91] appear to have lost their rounding brackets. That the displayed pair $(3/16)r + 7/8 \le t \le r/5$ is mutually satisfiable only for $r \ge 70$ was already observed in the working report at erdosproblemaday.com/report/616 (28 July 2026), which could not retrieve the paper to identify the cause. Reading the paper itself (JCTA 58 (1991) 78–84, Elsevier open archive) settles it: the prose after Theorem 3 and the Section 4 construction state $\lfloor (3/16)r + 7/8 \rfloor \le t \le \lceil r/5 \rceil$, which is consistent for all $r \ge 3$ — so the display here has dropped the floor and ceiling, and no range qualifier was ever needed. (Two immediate consequences of the bracketed reading: $t = 1$ for $r = 3, 4, 5$ — also forced by the Erdős–Gallai bound the paper cites as Theorem C — and $t(6) = t(7) = 2$, where floor equals ceiling.)
